title: Sensitive data exposure boundaries across public and diagnostic surfaces
purpose: Find reachable disclosures of credentials, secrets, tokens, private key material or explicitly sensitive configuration and audit payloads through public reads, logs, errors, diagnostics, telemetry, event and mirror outputs, backup/export artifacts, CLI rendering and Kubernetes operator surfaces. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract. Preparation of this P1 manifest does not authorize an audit: refresh the inventory and deduplication context after the active sensitive-projection and sink-diagnostic PR stack stabilizes, then obtain a separate execution decision. This domain owns confidentiality of representations and propagation paths, not caller authorization, filesystem path confinement, generic PII discovery, cryptographic policy or downstream compromise.
invariants: Every finding must identify a concrete sensitive value, its production ingress or persisted source, the exact transformations and serializers it crosses, the reachable output surface and the observer that receives it. A field name, broad path match, missing redaction helper or hypothetical logger call is not evidence of disclosure. Use the sensitivity taxonomy and complete evidence chain in companion contracts A and B.

Raw credentials and secrets must not appear in public HTTP or service gRPC responses, list/get/audit/log/config DTOs, public error messages or structured error metadata. Safe projections may retain non-sensitive identity and configured-presence semantics, but no alternate codec, nested oneof, pointer/value marshal path, local/forwarded execution or streaming element may bypass the projection selected at the response boundary (contract C).

Logs, panic recovery, correlation diagnostics, sink and mirror failure state, CLI diagnostics, traces, span events, resource attributes, metrics labels and profiling tags must not record raw sensitive values. Server-side diagnostics are not an exemption: errors may retain operational context only after sanitizing credentials in URLs, headers, driver errors, request/config objects and wrapping chains. High-cardinality payloads and user business data are in scope only when the repository explicitly treats them as sensitive or they contain the synthetic canary under test (contract D).

Audit entries, ledger logs, event payloads, mirror configuration and replicated configuration must preserve authoritative business meaning and integrity while exposing only the approved read projection. Redaction must occur on a detached representation and must not mutate chain-bound, signed, hashed, persisted or replayed bytes; audit verification and event delivery must continue to use the authoritative form where required (contract E).

Backup manifests, checkpoint/export content, restore diagnostics and support or operator-visible artifacts must not acquire sensitive runtime configuration merely because they serialize broad structs or errors. When credentials are intentionally part of durable business configuration needed for restore, the audit must distinguish authorized durable content from unintended public, diagnostic or metadata exposure and must prove the actual artifact and access surface. Path locality and archive containment remain owned by filesystem-confinement-contracts (contract F).

Kubernetes Secrets and purpose-built credential retrieval commands are intentional secret-bearing surfaces; ordinary CR spec/status, Events, Conditions, annotations, labels, ConfigMaps, pod environment values, controller logs and generic get/list/config commands must contain only references, public keys, hashes or documented presence markers. A finding must distinguish an authorized explicit secret read from an incidental disclosure caused by reconciliation, status/error propagation or rendering (contract G).

Redaction must be complete and non-reversible for every registered sensitive variant while preserving the minimum non-sensitive semantics promised by the surface. Placeholders, omission and presence booleans must not reveal the secret value through length, prefix, query string, encoded form, digest used as a public identifier or error echo. Equality hashes used only for internal rollout may exist, but exposing them requires an established contract and an analysis of offline-guessing risk (contract H).

Ownership follows the first confidentiality boundary that emits or retains the value, not the last transport that happens to carry it. Route authorization and scope enforcement belong to authentication-authorization-boundaries; HTTP/gRPC shape parity unrelated to secrecy belongs to api-boundary-contracts; sink acknowledgement and cursor correctness belong to event-delivery-contracts; root confinement belongs to filesystem-confinement-contracts. Cross-domain evidence is allowed, but duplicate the same root cause only when a distinct independently reachable disclosure mechanism remains (contract I).
adversarial_questions: What exact fields at this SHA carry cluster secrets, bearer/PAT tokens, OAuth client secrets, SASL passwords, webhook signing secrets, database/object-store credentials, private signing or TLS key material, credential-bearing URLs and sensitive audit/config payloads? Which are secret values, identifiers, public keys, paths or documented presence metadata under contract A?

For each registered HTTP and service gRPC read that can return ledger, mirror, sink, audit, log, cluster or configuration data, where is the safe projection applied? Can get versus list, HTTP versus gRPC, unary versus stream, local versus forwarded, success versus partial response, or protojson versus generated/custom JSON select the authoritative secret-bearing object instead?

Can a nested SinkConfig, MirrorSourceConfig, BackupStorage, caller snapshot, audit order, ledger log or protobuf oneof reveal a credential through an unhandled new variant? Do descriptor-driven, clone, reflection, text/debug string and alternate JSON/YAML encoders preserve the same deny-by-default rule?

Can constructor, connection, publish, flush, close, retry or shutdown errors from HTTP, Kafka, NATS, ClickHouse, Databricks, PostgreSQL, S3 or Azure include a credential-bearing DSN, URL, request header, driver config, response body or wrapped SDK error? Trace the exact error into sink status, API response, log, span and CLI output rather than assuming an upstream library redacts it.

Can invalid bearer, cluster-secret, webhook, response-signing, TLS, OIDC/JWKS or object-store inputs be echoed by parsing, validation, authentication failure, file-loading or connection diagnostics? Authorization outcome is out of scope; follow the failure only to determine whether the supplied secret becomes observable.

Do HTTP panic/unmapped-error handling and gRPC error encoding keep public responses generic while recording only safe server diagnostics? Can domain PublicErrorDetails, ErrorInfo metadata, correlation IDs, trace RecordError, panic values/stacks or routing wrappers retain a canary secret across one or two transport hops?

Can startup config rendering, debug logging, config export, support output, pprof/flight-recorder data, OpenTelemetry logs/resources/spans, Prometheus labels or Pyroscope tags serialize a whole config, environment value, CLI argument, URL or error containing a secret? Test both value and pointer marshaling and every enabled encoder rather than relying on one Marshal method.

Does producing a public audit/log/event/mirror projection mutate the authoritative protobuf, oneof, map, slice or aliased nested message? Compare deterministic audit/hash bytes and subsequent internal consumers before and after projection; a confidentiality fix that breaks chain integrity, replay or event delivery is not acceptable.

Do full and incremental backup artifacts, manifests, export segments or restore status/errors contain runtime credentials or secret-bearing configuration beyond the durable contract? Use a non-empty post-checkpoint delta when following audited configuration, but leave restore parity and filesystem containment to their owning domains.

Can operator reconciliation copy secret Data/StringData into a ConfigMap, CR status, Event, Condition message, annotation, label, generated manifest, command argument or log? Do generated CRDs and CLI printers expose only Secret references and public credential metadata except in the explicit get-key flow?

Can redaction be bypassed with empty versus non-empty states, malformed UTF-8, control characters, very long values, URL userinfo/query parameters, percent/base64/hex encoding, a value equal to the redaction placeholder, repeated fields, unknown protobuf fields or a future oneof variant? Require exact canary absence in every emitted byte sequence, not a visual inspection.

Is a claimed disclosure actually the same root cause already being changed or tracked by the active sensitive-projection/redaction stack, or a distinct production path? Conversely, did a shared fix cover only public reads while leaving sink diagnostics, telemetry, backup/export or operator rendering independently reachable?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: For malformed credential-bearing HTTP mirror URLs, exercise admission, real HTTPSource head and batch calls, worker logs, serialized MirrorSyncUpdate, FSM application and ledger progress reads. Require no network request and no password in diagnostics, including wrapped causes; retain the parsing-failure marker and ledger identity. Include invalid escapes, userinfo, control characters and invalid ports whose underlying parser error echoes input. Configuration/audit projections remain separate from diagnostic status containment.

These are optional diagnostics for a separately authorized later audit. Use only unique synthetic canary secrets and disposable local fixtures at the pinned clean HEAD. Do not use real credentials, contact production services, edit tracked files, implement fixes, or invoke audit/challenge/Jira orchestration from a leaf provider. Record exact commands, enabled build tags and surfaces observed; an unexecuted check remains a reproduction plan.

Build a field-to-surface matrix from current protobuf descriptors, Go configuration structs, registered sink/mirror/backup factories, HTTP routes, gRPC descriptors, CLI commands and operator CRDs. Seed each sensitive field with a distinct canary so a failure identifies the missing projection. Assert both absence of raw and encoded canaries and preservation of approved names, endpoints, types and configured-presence markers.

Exercise every current get/list/audit/log/config response through registered HTTP and gRPC servers, including local and forwarded controls where supported. Marshal returned messages with the actual wire codec and relevant alternate encoders; cover unary and streaming failures, nested oneofs, pointer/value forms and an unknown/future-variant simulation when the projection contract provides one.

Use fake local HTTP endpoints and existing sink test doubles for success, redirect, authentication rejection, malformed response, timeout and credential-bearing error text. For tagged Kafka/NATS/ClickHouse/Databricks implementations, use repository-provided containers or injectable constructors only when already supported; otherwise inspect reachable wrapping and state propagation and leave an exact test plan. Capture sink status, logs, spans and public responses independently.

Route synthetic sensitive errors through HTTP panic recovery, HTTP unmapped and KindInternal branches, gRPC status conversion, leader forwarding, cursor Recv failures, apierr decoding and CLI rendering. Pair each case with a non-sensitive diagnostic marker so an empty or swallowed error cannot pass. Inspect response bytes, structured log fields, ErrorInfo metadata and exported span events.

Marshal bootstrap configuration through every supported startup/debug encoder and inspect OpenTelemetry log/resource configuration, metric attributes, pprof/flight-recorder and Pyroscope tags with synthetic values in flags, environment variables, URLs and wrapped errors. Verify the original configuration remains unchanged after redaction and that absent/present state follows the documented contract.

Create disposable full and incremental backup fixtures containing a deliberately sensitive runtime config and a distinct legitimate business payload canary. Inspect manifest, checkpoint metadata, export segments and restore diagnostics without publishing or uploading them. Prove that the secret is absent unless an authoritative durability contract explicitly requires it, while the business payload remains round-trippable.

Use the operator fake client and existing env/StatefulSet/Credentials fixtures to reconcile synthetic Secrets and failing resources. Inspect CR spec/status, Events, Conditions, ConfigMaps, pod specs, annotations and captured controller logs. Separately assert that the explicit get-key command returns the requested secret to its authorized caller; that intentional output is a control, not a leak.

Run focused existing redaction, public-error, internal-diagnostic, sink failure, audit hash, event serialization, config export and operator credential tests discovered at the audited SHA. Existing green tests are evidence of specific paths only; they do not replace the descriptor/registration inventory or prove new variants are denied by default.

For operator backups, reconcile full and incremental BackupRuns with same-namespace S3 Secret references and serialize Backup, BackupRun, Job and Pod template as JSON/YAML. Require canary absence and retained bucket controls, non-optional secretKeyRef environment delivery, no S3 credentials in command/argv, and actual ledgerctl environment-to-storage-RPC mapping. Also exercise omitted references for the Ledger server default credential chain.
